charts.title: How the photon test was built: one burst, one fitted slope, a shuffle control and a planted delay.
charts.takeaway: 84 photons gave a slope of 0 ms per GeV, bounded at 117 ms per GeV, which is 0.321 Planck energies.
charts.n: 84 photons in the analysis window, from 119 above 100 MeV near the burst

steps.label: 1,214,533 photons in the weekly file
steps.detail: Fermi Large Area Telescope public archive, the week that holds GRB 090510.

steps.label: 119 near the burst, 84 in the window
steps.detail: Above 100 MeV, 1 s before to 3 s after the trigger. The top photon has 29.9 GeV and arrived at 0.828 s.

steps.label: Fit the delay slope
steps.detail: Shift each photon back by slope times energy and keep the slope that bunches arrival times most tightly. Fitted slope: 0 ms per GeV.

steps.label: Shuffle the energies, 300 times
steps.detail: Breaks any link between energy and arrival time. Shuffled slopes ran from −44 to +76 ms per GeV.

steps.label: Plant a known delay
steps.detail: Delays of 1, 3, 5 and 10 times the bound were added and refitted. Largest error: 0.9 percent.

steps.label: Rule: speed change below 1e−15 of c
steps.detail: Set before the run: with a slope consistent with zero, this ends the vacuum form in the tested band.

steps.label: No energy-dependent speed found
steps.detail: Speed change below 7.6e−18 of c at 29.9 GeV. The bound is weaker than the published one.

charts.title: The fitted delay slope against the range that shuffled energies give.
charts.takeaway: The real slope is 0 ms per GeV, inside the shuffled range of −44 to +76; its resampling interval reaches −117, which sets the bound of 117.
charts.units: delay slope in milliseconds per GeV: how much later a photon arrives for each GeV of energy; zero means no energy-dependent speed
charts.n: 84 photons in the analysis window, from 119 above 100 MeV near the burst; 300 resamples for the interval and 300 shuffles for the control
charts.interval: 2.5th to 97.5th percentile of the slope refitted on photons resampled with replacement (a bootstrap)
charts.baseline: Photon energies shuffled among the same photons and the slope refitted, 300 times
charts.threshold: Real slope inside the shuffled range, and a planted delay of 5 times the bound recovered within 20 percent
charts.planted: Held: planted delays of 1, 3, 5 and 10 times the bound came back within 0.9 percent

axis.label: delay slope, ms per GeV (zero means no energy-dependent speed)

regions.label: slopes with energies shuffled, 2.5th to 97.5th percentile

charts.title: Lower limits on the energy scale where light speed could start to depend on photon energy.
charts.takeaway: Our plain rerun reaches 0.321 Planck energies and the published analysis of the same burst reaches 7.6, about 24 times stronger. A longer bar is a stronger limit.
charts.units: linear energy scale in Planck energies (the Planck energy is about 1.22e19 GeV); the limit says any linear effect must lie above this scale, so higher is stronger
charts.n: 84 photons in the analysis window, from 119 above 100 MeV near the burst; published values are quoted in the result file from the papers' abstracts
charts.no_interval: Each bar is itself a 95 percent lower limit; the result file holds no interval on a limit.
charts.baseline: Published limits: 7.6 Planck energies from GRB 090510 and 10 from GRB 221009A
charts.threshold: Forecast set in advance: our limit between 0.5 and 10 Planck energies. The resampling bound fell below it.

axis.label: lower limit on the linear energy scale, Planck energies (longer is stronger)

charts.title: Wave speed in the simulated condensate against wavenumber: sound has a speed limit that bends at short wavelength.
charts.takeaway: Long waves move at the sound speed (ratio 0.982); at the shortest wave tested the measured phase speed is 2.24 times the sound speed, on the Bogoliubov law within 1.9 percent at every point.
charts.units: speed in units of the sound speed; phase speed is frequency divided by wavenumber, group speed is the speed of a wave packet
charts.n: 6 wavenumbers in one simulated condensate; a wave packet at short wavelength moved at 2.89 times the sound speed
charts.no_interval: One deterministic simulation per wavenumber; the result file holds each point's error against the law, shown in the table.
charts.baseline: The Bogoliubov law (the known link between frequency and wavenumber for small waves in a condensate) and the sound speed, 1
charts.threshold: Measured frequency within 2 percent of the law at every wavenumber; group speed above 1.1 where wavenumber times healing length is 1

x.label: wavenumber times healing length (the length below which the condensate stops acting like a fluid)

y.label: speed, in units of the sound speed

charts.title: Every verdict set in advance, the value it tested and the bar it had to clear.
charts.takeaway: 12 of 15 held. The 3 that failed are two forecasts of how strong our own bound would be and the packet's lag near the simulated horizon.
charts.units: each row states its own quantity; sound rows are in units where the sound speed is 1
charts.n: 15 verdicts built from 23 rules; 84 photons in the analysis window, from 119 above 100 MeV near the burst
charts.no_interval: Each rule compares one value with one bar fixed before the run.
